channel.title: Molecular & Cell Biology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Cell Biology, Molecular Cell, Nature Structural & Molecular Biology, and The EMBO Journal.

item.title: Molecular Cell: A lysosomal DRAM1-GLUT1-NADPH axis coordinates glucose sensing with metabolic reprogramming
item.description: Li et al. identify a lysosome-based feedback system that helps cells adapt to excess glucose. High glucose increases DRAM1 and NADPH, promoting GLUT1 retention at lysosomes, reducing glucose entry and glycolysis, and shifting cells toward greater reliance on glutamine to fuel metabolism.

item.title: Molecular Cell: A sequence-encoded promoter-proximal super pause stabilizes an offline RNA polymerase II state
item.description: Vazquez Nunez et al. develop GATO-seq, a cell-free genomics method to directly measure RNA polymerase II elongation dynamics. They identify a “super pause” DNA sequence near gene start sites that alone potently pauses RNA polymerase II, trapping it in a yet undescribed “sidetracked” conformation, showing how DNA sequence itself controls pausing.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: TF-MAPS: fast high-resolution functional and allosteric mapping of DNA-binding proteins
item.description: Li and Lehner present TF-MAPS, a scalable platform to chart functional maps of sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins. The authors map allostery in three transcription factors implicated in human disease and reveal potentially druggable small pockets.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: GPCR-MAPS: high-resolution functional and allosteric mapping of G-protein-coupled receptor activation functions and bias
item.description: Mighell and Lehner present GPCR-MAPS, which enables scalable functional mapping of G-protein-coupled receptors. They obtained measurements across multiple phenotypes of the β 2 adrenergic receptor to reveal a modular activation architecture and determinants of signaling bias, prioritizing undrugged allosteric sites.

item.title: Molecular Cell: The C-terminal tail of the RBR E3 ligase RNF14 defines branched K6/K48 polyubiquitin specificity in ribosomal quality control
item.description: Trevelyan et al. report that the E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF14 forms branched K6/K48 polyubiquitin and identify RNF14’s C-terminal tail as a critical component for its chain-type and branching activity. This work opens research avenues for branched K6/K48 ubiquitin in ribosomal quality control and the biological functions of branched ubiquitin.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Hierarchical buffering of cellular RNA polymerase II pools maintains transcriptional homeostasis
item.description: Gillis et al. integrate quantitative single-cell imaging with genomic techniques to examine transcriptional homeostasis following acute perturbation of RNA polymerase II abundance. This work demonstrates that total mRNA production is buffered against altered polymerase abundance by the transcription cycle and further shows evidence for robustness in RNA polymerase holoenzyme assembly.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Dot1 triggers a conserved ribophagy signal to govern ribosome quality and longevity by methylating Rpl12
item.description: Chen et al. show Dot1-mediated Rpl12 methylation as a conserved autophagic “eat-me” signal that directs selective ribosome degradation. By coupling nutrient sensing to ribosome quality control, this mechanism promotes cellular adaptation to stress, maintains tissue homeostasis, and supports organismal longevity.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Promoter-proximal pausing enables transcriptional buffering of RNA polymerase II availability
item.description: Through titration of cellular RPB1 levels, Olthof et al. show that transcription is surprisingly sensitive to RNAPII dosage, but that genes vary widely in their sensitivity. Genes involved in transcriptional maintenance are typically dosage insensitive. Expression of these genes is buffered through decreased promoter-proximal pausing and increased mRNA stability.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Association of AXIN1 assemblies with microtubules inhibits Wnt/β-catenin signaling
Molecular Cell: Nuclear TRiC states captured in situ
item.description: Xing et al. visualize the duty cycle of nuclear TRiC using cryo-electron tomography and identify TRiC interactors in the nucleus. These findings indicate that TRiC may act on misfolded proteins in the nucleus.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Identification and regulation of an ACC1-associated lipogenic metabolon in liver
item.description: Zhu et al. identify a nutrient-responsive ACC1-centered metabolon that organizes lipid-synthesis enzymes near lipid droplets and associates with intracellular trafficking proteins. ACC1-associated interactions increase in steatotic, insulin-resistant livers, revealing a potential target for modulating hepatic lipid production in MASLD.

item.title: Molecular Cell: PARP1 hyperactivation uncouples transcription from protein expression through nuclear RNA retention
item.description: Ortega et al. show that PARP1 hyperactivation suppresses translation by promoting nuclear RNA retention. APE1-dependent cleavage of abasic sites triggers PARP1 hyperactivation, increasing nuclear PAR, which competes with RNA for binding to RNA-binding proteins. This disrupts RNA splicing and export, limiting expression of DNA damage-induced stress-response proteins.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: E2F1 induces a G0-G1 reentry transcriptional program without changing chromatin accessibility
Nature Cell Biology: Tau monomers and fibrils escape microglial clearance via distinct cellular mechanisms
item.description: Kulkarni et al. show distinct fates of monomeric versus fibrillar tau in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia. Monomeric tau is internalized but does not reach degradative lysosomes; fibrillar tau adheres to the cell surface and triggers microglial activation.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Positional replication fork instability drives PARP inhibitor cytotoxicity
item.description: Through CRISPR screens and single-molecule imaging, Gupta et al. show that loss of the cohesion acetyltransferase ESCO2 leads to increased G-quadruplex formation at specific regions and drives PARP activation and PARPi hypersensitivity.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Bacterial 2′,3′-cGAMP signaling induces membrane splitting in antiphage CBASS immunity
item.description: Li et al. reveal how the bacterial CdnB-Cap14 CBASS pathway converts DNA sensing into membrane-disrupting antiphage defense. DNA activates autoinhibited CdnB to produce 2′,3′-cGAMP in vitro, which induces Cap14 filament assembly and partitions the membrane into two layers. Phage Acb2 counteracts this pathway by sequestering 2′,3′-cGAMP and blocking signal transmission.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Large-scale RNA-binding protein tethering screen discovers modulators of circular RNA metabolism
item.description: This study systematically evaluates proteins that control circular RNA production, stability and translation, revealing new regulators and strategies to enhance or suppress circular RNA activity for therapeutic development.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Tetraspanin CD81 restricts Ebola virus infection and is antagonized by glycoprotein GP and matrix protein VP40
Nature Cell Biology: STING-dependent TNF signalling promotes IKKβ-mediated ATG9A phosphorylation and autophagy
item.description: Chen, Zhong et al. show that cGAS−STING activation upon chemotherapy treatment leads to TNF expression. Paracrine TNF signalling leads to IKKβ-dependent phosphorylation of ATG9A and autophagy, promoting chemotherapy resistance.

item.title: Molecular Cell: A TORC1-regulated H3K4me reader preserves promoter chromatin stability, and its degradation promotes meiotic remodeling
item.description: Yun et al. show that Jmj3 and Lid2 preserve H3K4-methylated promoter chromatin by restricting NuA4-dependent remodeling. Under low-nutrient conditions, TORC1 inactivation drives Ubc14-Dbl4-mediated degradation of Jmj3/Lid2, allowing promoter remodeling that coordinates meiotic gene expression with Rec12-dependent recombination.

item.title: Molecular Cell: The chromatin context differently impacts prime editors and base editors and controls the fidelity and purity of base editing
item.description: Wang, Zittersteijn et al. show that the chromatin landscape of a target sequence is a key determinant of DSB-free genome-editing outcomes. Strikingly, while heterochromatin often impairs prime editing, it can enhance base editing and additionally control the fidelity and purity of the DNA modification products generated.

item.title: Molecular Cell: P-TEFb regulates nucleosome positioning at promoters
item.description: P-TEFb/SEC releases paused RNA Pol II, but its role in chromatin organization is less clear. Guo et al. show that SEC directly phosphorylates CHD1, maintaining nucleosome positioning in the early elongation zone and coupling chromatin remodeling to efficient transcription elongation. PILBOS-linked CHD1-CTD mutations disrupt promoter-proximal nucleosome positioning and transcription elongation.

item.title: Molecular Cell: An SMN2 splicing-correcting antisense oligonucleotide promotes gene looping and transcription activation
item.description: Splicing-correcting antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) are powerful therapeutic tools for hereditary diseases. Stigliano, Haberfeld, et al. found that ASOs not only correct faulty mRNA splicing but also promote physical contacts between the two ends of the targeted gene. This gene looping activates transcription, which adds a beneficial layer to ASOs, expanding their therapeutic potential.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Ca2+ is an intracellular danger signal promoting STING activation
item.description: The biological significance of Ca2+ signaling on STING remains unclear. Zhou et al. show that Ca2+ is an immediate-early danger signal promoting STING activation. Viral infection-activated Rho GTPases trigger IP3 induced, while STING translocation activates TRPV2-mediated ER Ca2+ release. Both lead to CaMK1D activation, which subsequently phosphorylates STING for TBK1 activation.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Safe lysosomal sequestration of ferrous iron is mediated via cholesterol shielding and drives senescence and ferroptosis resistance
The EMBO Journal: CDC7 and CDK8 kinases cooperate to support DNA replication origin firing in human cells
The EMBO Journal: Comprehensive proteomic profiling reveals mRNA splicing suppression during human oocyte aging
Nature Cell Biology: Phase separation of SMARCAL1 orchestrates epigenetic reprogramming and methionine metabolism to foster radioresistance and immunosuppression
item.description: Zheng, Cui, Li et al. demonstrate a role for SMARCAL1 in modulating histone lactylation and chromatin remodelling via phase separation, thereby impacting the antitumour efficacy of radiotherapy and immunotherapy.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Structural basis for the non-canonical nucleosome remodeling by ATRX
item.description: Wang et al. show that ATRX remodels chromatin through an unusual mechanism that favors nucleosome disassembly over repositioning. ATRX also captures histones and cooperates with ASF1 for tetrasome assembly, linking chromatin remodeling to histone chaperoning for reassembly and helping explain how ATRX functions at accessible chromatin regions.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: EMC chaperone activity is required for cotranslational calcium channel assembly
item.description: Stanton et al. show that the human endoplasmic reticulum membrane protein complex (EMC) engages nascent calcium channels cotranslationally as a chaperone as part of a large ribosome–multipass translocon–EMC supercomplex. Loss of this function impairs channel biogenesis and disrupts cardiomyocyte contraction.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: ATAD2B governs epigenetic silencing of the epithelial program to fuel cancer metastasis and neuronal migration
Nature Cell Biology: Methylated eEF1A selectively decodes mRNA to shape cancer proteomes
item.description: The authors show that METTL13-mediated eEF1A K55 dimethylation enhances decoding of rare codons, boosting translation of oncogenic proteins including KRAS and promoting KRAS-inhibitor resistance in lung cancer.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Tubulin acetylation regulates nuclear shape fluctuations and DNA repair
item.description: Wallis, Tse et al. propose that DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) induce microtubule acetylation, affecting nuclear shape and promoting DNA DSB mobility.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Motile vesicles (MoVes) are a cancer cell migration-associated extracellular vesicle population
item.description: Tsering et al. describe a class of extracellular vesicles called motile vesicles (MoVes) that is produced by migrating cancer cells, contains genomic DNA and includes organelles that can be transferred to recipient cells.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural mechanism of programmable gene integration by the R2 retrotransposon coupled with CRISPR–Cas9
item.description: Here, the authors determine the cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Taeniopygia guttata R2 retrotransposon complex, both alone and bound to a CRISPR–Cas9 complex, providing a framework for engineering R2-based gene integration technologies.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: A nanoscale map of the human cell surface proteome reveals spatial and functional organization
item.description: Floyd et al. use proximity labeling, mass spectrometry and machine learning to map the spatial organization of the human surfaceome, revealing functional protein modules, surface-localized mitochondrial proteins and regulators of immune signaling.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Modeling long-range human nigrostriatal connectivity in vitro reveals striatal target-dependent maturation of dopamine neurons
The EMBO Journal: Cis -regulatory co-option of a transposon family reinforces cell identity across the immune system
The EMBO Journal: Root endophyte sulfur metabolites enhance redox balance and drought tolerance in Arabidopsis
Molecular Cell: The 9-1-1 complex protects ssDNA gaps in BRCA2-deficient cancer
item.description: Grimsley et al. demonstrate that the 9-1-1 complex safeguards BRCA2-deficient cells from lethal ssDNA gap accumulation by suppressing PRIMPOL-dependent gap formation, restraining EXO1 degradation, and promoting POLζ-mediated filling. This identifies an ATR-independent 9-1-1 role in post-replicative repair and establishes gap length as a key determinant of repair pathway choice.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Amyloid-mediated RNA uptake by sperm for embryonic delivery
item.description: Semen carries extracellular RNA that shapes early embryonic development, but how it reaches sperm is unclear. Mallen et al. show that amyloid fibrils in seminal fluid bind RNA, enter sperm, and deliver their cargo to the zygote at fertilization, where chaperones release it for translation.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Differential roles for the spindle assembly checkpoint in error surveillance and mitotic timing
Nature Cell Biology: Keratin 9 regulates mechanosensitive YAP1 signalling in palmoplantar epidermis
item.description: Steiner et al. propose that keratin 9 (K9) interacts with 14-3-3, sequestering YAP1 in the cytoplasm and inhibiting YAP1 activity. They identify dysregulated YAP in palmoplantar keratinization diseases, with K9 as a downstream regulator of YAP.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: The rapid delivery of RNase H variants reveals distinct classes of RNA:DNA hybrids
Nature Cell Biology: The rise of reducing reagent-resistant TfR1 dimer marks ferroptosis
item.description: He et al. report the upregulation of a reducing reagent-resistant form of the transferrin receptor 1 dimer during lipid peroxidation and demonstrate its utility in detecting ferroptosis in tissue lysates and extracellular vesicles from mice and humans.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Protein arginine methylation promotes global 3′UTR shortening in proliferating cells
item.description: Griffith et al. show that arginine methylation drives production of short mRNA isoforms in rapidly dividing cells by enabling PCF11 to assemble productively into the cleavage and polyadenylation machinery. PRMT inhibition globally lengthens 3′UTRs across cancer cells, organoids, and T cells, revealing a targetable link between methylation and alternative polyadenylation.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Architecture of the Norrin signaling complex and structure-guided surrogate design
item.description: Hu, Li et al. uncover how Norrin assembles Frizzled 4, tetraspanin 12 and low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 5 into a signaling complex and use this structural insight to design potent Norrin surrogates, providing a framework for developing therapies for retinal vascular diseases.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: DZIP3 is a viral RNA co-sensor for RIG-I that promotes type-I interferon responses
The EMBO Journal: Non-random inter-speckle material transfer mediated by dynamic multiphase interchromatin connections
The EMBO Journal: Activator mimicry by PP6 regulatory subunits directs Aurora A dephosphorylation in mitosis
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Mechanism of M18BP1-mediated activation of condensin II for mitotic DNA compaction
item.description: Here, the authors show that phosphorylated M18BP1 activates condensin II by relieving an autoinhibitory interface, enabling stable DNA binding and compaction. Additionally, the M18BP1–condensin II complex forms clusters that might mechanically reinforce mitotic chromosomes.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Monocyte surface Y RNAs potentiate innate immunity
item.description: Jiang, He, Xu, Zheng et al. report a functional role for cell-surface Y RNAs in modulating extracellular histone-induced inflammatory signalling and cytokine secretion, which may contribute to the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: ATP-driven dynamics and itraconazole binding of the drug efflux pump Cdr1 from Candida glabrata
The EMBO Journal: Golgi-associated tethers capture vesicles from specific membrane recycling pathways
The EMBO Journal: A USP28-TM9SF3-Golgiphagy axis maintains glycosylation homeostasis and promotes breast cancer progression
The EMBO Journal: Microtubule pushing and cortical pulling cooperate to orient and position the mitotic spindle
The EMBO Journal: Electrostatic control of chromatin compaction safeguards against apoptotic DNA release
Molecular Cell: Molecular mechanism of residue-specific nucleosome acetylation
item.description: Müller, Kolesnikova, Doudin, et al. reveal a structural mechanism for residue-specific nucleosome acetylation by capturing the MSL histone acetyltransferase during catalysis. Their findings provide a foundation for understanding how H4K16 acetylation links transcription to changes in chromatin structure, a mechanism essential for Drosophila dosage compensation and implicated in human disease.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Alternative splicing fine-tunes modular protein interfaces to control protein localization
item.description: Kjer-Hansen et al. show that alternative splicing reshapes how proteins interact and where they localize in cells, with tiny microexons making a disproportionate contribution to protein organization and cellular function.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Proximity of pre-mRNA 3′ end processing and transcription termination is associated with enhanced gene expression
The EMBO Journal: Uncovering essential RNA components of fusion oncoprotein condensates using bicon-seq
Molecular Cell: Structural basis of directionality control in large serine integrases
item.description: Shin et al. present cryo-EM structures of the SPβ integrase along the integration and excision pathways that provide mechanistic insights addressing the long-standing questions of how large serine integrases enforce highly directional DNA recombination and how the cognate recombination directionality factor leads to a complete reversal of directionality.

item.title: Molecular Cell: A feedback mechanism of m6A via PARP1-mediated ADP ribosylation of METTL3/METTL14
item.description: Bai et al. reveal a PARP1-mediated m6A feedback mechanism involving IGF2BPs and the METTL3/METTL14 writer complex. They further show that combined targeting of ADP ribosylation and m6A leads to synergistic anti-tumor effects, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Ligand-dependent G protein dynamics underlying opioid efficacy
item.description: Deutsch et al. show how μ-opioid receptor agonists exert long-range allosteric control over bound G proteins, providing an additional mechanism for encoding opioid signaling outcomes.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural basis of an endoplasmic reticulum EMC:Spf1 insertase–dislocase complex
item.description: Klose et al. provide structural insights into a supercomplex between the EMC and Spf1 that brings together cellular machines for membrane protein insertion and extraction into a single entity, providing a framework for integrated membrane protein quality control.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Three-dimensional mechanical cooperativity optimises epithelial wound healing
The EMBO Journal: Expression patterns of CD24 and CD27 resolve the origins and gradual differentiation of CD11c + atypical memory B-cells after malaria infection
The EMBO Journal: Switch from canonical to recombination-dependent DNA synthesis by M-CDK phosphorylation of DNA Polα
The EMBO Journal: The miR-744-5p/connexin 43 axis modulates Salmonella -containing vacuole association with the Golgi network
The EMBO Journal: Dynamics of bicoid mRNA localisation and translation dictate morphogen gradient formation
Nature Cell Biology: In vivo DNA damage protection during cell migration across confining embryonic tissue environments
item.description: Häkkinen et al. show that zebrafish neural crest cells encounter increased tissue-scale confinement along the body axis. Despite nuclear deformation, migrating neural crest cells experience neither nuclear envelope rupture nor increased DNA damage.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Power-law scaling of mitotic spindles with genome sizes across eukaryotes is driven by chromosome crowding
item.description: Gudlin, Vukušić, Novak and colleagues propose spindle scaling in response to chromosome crowding consistent across eukaryotes. They show that metaphase plate width scales with genome size following a power law with an exponent of ~1/3.

item.title: Molecular Cell: 40S ribosome remodeling triggers 18S rRNA U-tailing and DIS3L2-dependent decay
item.description: Translational perturbations trigger ubiquitination and turnover of 40S ribosomes, yet how these events are coupled remains unclear. Shah et al. reveal that RIOK3 remodels ubiquitinated 40S subunits, exposing the 3′ end of 18S rRNA for uridylation and subsequent DIS3L2-mediated degradation. These findings link ribosomal protein ubiquitination to selective rRNA turnover.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Oligo(uridine) tailing and exonucleolytic decay drive 40S ribosome degradation in response to stress
item.description: 40S ribosomes are degraded in diverse stress conditions. Diehl et al. find that in response to stress, TUT7 is recruited to ubiquitylated 40S ribosomes and adds 3′ oligo(U) tails to the 18S rRNA. Iterative uridylation and 3′-5′ decay by the exonuclease DIS3L2 drive 18S rRNA and ultimately 40S ribosome degradation.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Mechanistic insights into chromatin modulation by the “orphan” remodeler ATRX
item.description: Duan et al. solved the structure of ATRX ATPase-nucleosome complex, uncovering three distinctive features that enable ATRX to remodel nucleosomes. These newly identified features are indispensable for protecting cells from G4 stress. The work provides a framework for interpreting both known and future mutations linked to ATRX-related disorders.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Reciprocal coupling between EMT and BMP morphogen signalling drives collective cell invasion
Molecular Cell: A genome-scale adaptation map identifies the FANCM-RMI1/2 complex as an opposing modulator of cell fitness upon BRCA1 or BRCA2 loss
item.description: Dossin et al. report that BRCA1 and BRCA2 deficiencies create distinct adaptive states. They identify FANCM-RMI1/2 as an opposing determinant of cell fitness: essential in BRCA1-deficient cells but toxic in BRCA2-deficient cells, where it drives replication fork degradation. Disrupting FANCM-RMI1/2 restores genome stability and promotes PARPi resistance in BRCA2-deficient cells.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Global and specific mechanisms stimulate mistranslation in cancer
item.description: Wernaart, Fumagalli et al. report ADAR1 and FTSJ1 as regulators of tryptophan-to-phenylalanine substitution in cancer. ADAR1 sustains mistranslation via ribosome quality control. FTSJ1 methylates tRNATrp and allows tRNATrp mischarging by phenylalanine.

item.title: Molecular Cell: An epigenetic program dictates MYC amplification dynamics that promote transient, extrachromosomal, and inherited genomic events
item.description: Ferman et al. demonstrate that epigenetic imbalance directly controls MYC oncogene amplification dynamics, which identifies possible biomarkers and therapeutic targets for aggressive tumors. When a cell-death checkpoint fails, the low MYC copy gains expand to high levels, which include circular and integrated events and associate with tumorigenesis.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Single-molecule chromatin tracing reveals a diversity of megabase heterochromatin domains
item.description: Single-molecule imaging reveals diverse, megabase-scale heterochromatin domains in C. elegans . Some resemble TADs and depend on condensin I; others are independent of condensin and histone H3K9me, including one domain that encloses the 5S rDNA locus.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: A conserved archaeal protein with evolutionary links to bacterial ribosome hibernation and eukaryotic energy sensing
The EMBO Journal: A dual-action bacteriophage protein Ped1 degrades DNA and blocks replication in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
The EMBO Journal: Leptin-sensitive hypothalamic Lepr+/Glp1r + neurons limit hyperphagia and weight gain in diet-induced obesity
Nature Cell Biology: Quantification of lipid sorting during clathrin-mediated endocytosis
item.description: Lennartz et al. evaluate lipid enrichment in clathrin-coated pits and observe that the differential lipid partitioning into clathrin-coated pits is largely driven by the lipid asymmetry of the plasma membrane.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Cotranslational membrane protein biogenesis by an EMC-bound translocon
item.description: The authors use selective ribosome profiling, cryo-ET and site-specific photocrosslinking to show how the ER membrane protein complex (EMC) cooperates with ribosome-bound translocons to facilitate multipass membrane protein biogenesis in human cells.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Profiling extracellular vesicle glycoRNAs defines their function in vesicular communication
item.description: The authors expand the extracellular vesicle glycosylated RNA (glycoRNA) landscape and reveal distinct glycoRNA profiles across extracellular vesicle (EV) subtypes, cell types and passage numbers. They also show that glycoRNAs are not only EV cargoes but also regulators of EV uptake, uncovering a layer of vesicle-mediated communication.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: HERC4-mediated ubiquitination licenses RIPK1 to initiate TNF-induced cell death
item.description: Lu and Du et al. show that HERC4 E3 ligase ubiquitinates S166-phosphorylated RIPK1 to initiate prodeath complex assembly and TNF-induced cell death, acting as the pivotal prodeath switch and that loss of HERC4 protects mice from TNF-driven inflammation and liver injury.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: MCM10 and SLD-2/RECQL4 jointly activate the CMG helicase during metazoan DNA replication initiation
The EMBO Journal: Excess Met1-linked ubiquitination leads to solid aggregate formation
The EMBO Journal: A functional screen for bacterial ubiquitin regulation identifies an unusual Pseudomonas aeruginosa E3 ligase
The EMBO Journal: Clustering of host N-glycans by the microneme MIC1/4/6 complex licenses Toxoplasma rhoptry discharge
Nature Cell Biology: Taxane-induced conformational changes in the microtubule lattice activate GEF-H1-dependent RhoA signalling
item.description: Meiring, Mahapatra et al. show that expanded microtubule lattice conformations, such as those induced by small-molecule taxanes, can lead to the release of GEF-H1 and thus induce RhoA activation.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Whole genome duplication through mitotic slippage causes nuclear instability
The EMBO Journal: Transgenerational inheritance of altered H3K27me3 in wild-type Caenorhabditis elegans
The EMBO Journal: The BRCA1 coiled-coil domain is dispensable for suppression of tandem duplications and tolerance of FANCM loss
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Mechanistic insights into phosphorylation-driven activation and therapeutic inhibition of human ATR–ATRIP
item.description: Wang et al. present cryo-electron microscopy structures of ATR–ATRIP complexes in distinct functional states, revealing ATP-dependent and TopBP1-dependent mechanisms of kinase activation and how ATR inhibitors exploit ATP-binding pocket flexibility for selective inhibition.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: ZEP1 orchestrates template choice and crossover pathways to ensure meiotic genome integrity in rice
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structure-guided discovery and engineering of miniature CRISPR–Cas12m for epigenome editing
item.description: The authors identified and engineered a miniature, innate nuclease-dead xCas12m enabling effective epigenome editing. xCas12m–CRISPRoff achieved durable epigenetic silencing and inhibition of hepatitis B virus infection through single-AAV delivery.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: The Batten disease protein CLN8 is a stereospecific acyltransferase in bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate biosynthesis
item.description: Two studies show that the endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein CLN8 catalyses the acyl CoA-dependent acylation of glycerophosphoglycerol, producing lysophosphatidylglycerol, which is then converted into bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate. These results provide insight into CLN8 Batten disease.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Batten disease protein CLN8 enables a non-canonical phospholipid synthesis pathway
item.description: Two studies show that the ER-associated protein CLN8 catalyses the acyl CoA-dependent acylation of glycerophosphoglycerol, producing lysophosphatidylglycerol, which is then converted into BMP. These results provide insight into CLN8 Batten disease.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: DFCP1-containing ER microdomains mediate lysosomal membrane repair
item.description: Radulovic et al. show that phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P), produced by the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase PIK3C3, is formed on ER domains after lysosome damage. ER domain PI3P helps to recruit the ATPase DFCP1, which promotes lysosome repair.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Hox / Meis -dependent gene-regulatory transition underlies cardiopharyngeal neural crest diversification
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Cryo-EM structure, enzymatic activity and genome targeting of canonical PRC1
item.description: Ciapponi et al. determine the cryo-electron microscopy structure of the canonical Polycomb repressive complex 1 holocomplex and show how its architecture coordinates complex assembly, H2A monoubiquitination and genomic targeting.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Microtubule posttranslational modifications provide unique recognition patterns for associated proteins
Nature Cell Biology: 4D nucleome landscape reveals dissolution of bipartite active X chromosome in liver cancer development
item.description: Xie, Tan, Mo and colleagues show that a liver-specific bipartite structure of the active X chromosome is lost early in hepatocarcinogenesis in mice and humans, driving X-linked gene activation and premalignant transformation, particularly in males.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Gain-of-function suppressors restore microtubule dynamics and rescue dominant-negative tubulinopathies
item.description: Xu, Guo et al. report suppressor screens in Caenorhabditis elegans to counteract tubulin mutants. They report several missense variants in tubulin genes that may restore microtubule architecture and dynamics, which may have some conservation in mammalian cells.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: ATP-independent unfolding of ubiquitin by Ufd1 initiates Cdc48/p97-mediated substrate processing
item.description: Wang et al. show that the UT3 domain of Ufd1 binds to and unfolds K48-linked polyubiquitin chains without ATP. Simultaneous binding of two ubiquitins to UT3 is key to overcome the energy barrier. This ubiquitin unfolding is critical for Cdc48/p97’s function.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Pre-activation and gating pathway of AMPA receptors revealed by full and partial agonists
item.description: AMPA receptor (AMPAR) gating proceeds through an intermediate pre-active state that has structurally remained an enigma. Here, Newton et al. use full and partial agonists and time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy to resolve this state and reveal the complete gating pathway of AMPARs.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: KDM6A loss enhances oxidative phosphorylation uncovering tissue-level convergent evolution
The EMBO Journal: Presynaptic accumulation of APP-CTFβ may contribute to synaptic dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease
